name: DataVolt Oxagon AI data centre campus (NEOM)
summary: Saudi developer DataVolt plans a 1.5 GW AI data centre campus at Oxagon, NEOM's industrial city on the Red Sea coast, on land leased from Oxagon. Under the February 2025 agreement DataVolt committed an initial USD 5 billion to the first phase, which is meant to run on renewable power. In August 2026 DataVolt and HUMAIN broke ground on a jointly developed 100 MW block within a 360 MW first phase, with the first 100 MW expected in service in 2028. Semafor reported in September 2026 that the initial facility would cost about USD 1 billion, and DataVolt's chief executive said the compute would be sold to customers abroad.

power_sources.description: The 2025 agreement says the campus is to run on renewable energy and operate at net zero, and the 2026 releases say it will integrate renewable sources; Oxagon is promoted as offering cost-competitive renewables and green hydrogen, but no specific supply has been named.

notes: Customer plans differ by source: DataVolt's release says the campus will serve international and domestic customers, while its chief executive told Semafor all capacity would be sold abroad. The August 2026 company releases disclose no investment figure for the 100 MW block; the only figure is Semafor's own estimate. DataVolt's chief executive also said project financing for the first facility was close to being secured.
